item.title: Lancaster Breakfast and History Walking Tour — Tue Nov 24, 9:00 AM — Unique Lancaster
item.description:
Searching for a walking history tour in Lancaster? You’re in for a flavorful experience—literally!
Introducing the Lancaster History & Breakfast Walking Tour—a dynamic two-hour adventure that blends the rich heritage of one of America’s oldest inland cities with a delicious morning meal. Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century.
Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI.
But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region.

item.description: Interact with Amish families in their homes and learn about their heritage while sampling homemade cookies. This holiday season, make new friends, learn new recipes, and create memories to last a lifetime. Take a step away from the stress of the holidays, slow down, and let us take you on a relaxing and festive journey. We will visit three authentic Amish homes to sample homemade Christmas cookies. item.title: Ben Franklin Bridge 38 miles F RSVP required — Fri Nov 27, 11:00 AM
item.description:
Lancaster Bicycle Club (LBC) Meetup Join a limited number of bicycle friends from the Wilmington and Lancaster clubs on a ride over the Ben Franklin Bridge.
We will park our cars at the Malvern SEPTA Train Station, 61 North Warren Ave, Malvern, leaving to ride at 11am. We will ride down Bridge Street pass Wegman’s and jump on the Chester Valley Trail. In Norristown the trail connects to the Schuylkill River Trail, which we will ride to the Art Museum in the city. After the Art Museum, we will connect to Race Street, ride Race Street across the city to 5th Street that will lead us to the bridge. After crossing the bridge we will ride to a park where we can take pictures of Philadelphia across the river. Coming back across the bridge, we will ride down Arch Street to the Reading Market where we will lock our bikes while we stop to eat. After eating we will ride to the Suburban Station, 15th & JFK. At the station you will need a SEPTA pass or purchase one. The fare should be around $8.00

item.title: Needle Felting Wreath Making Workshop (Adult Event) — Sat Dec 5, 3:00 PM — The Felted Fox
item.description:
Join us for a festive holiday workshop where we’ll be needle felting stars and using them and other decorations to arrange our very own wreaths! This beginner-friendly class will introduce you to the basics of needle felting as we transform soft wool into snowflake-esque stars. We will then fill in grapevine wreaths with our handmade felt stars, winter greenery, pinecones and bows!
This will be an adults-only workshop, for ages 21+. Participants may bring their own food and alcoholic or n/a beverages to enjoy during the workshop.
Warning: This event involves the use of sharp needles. Alcohol impairs motor skills and coordination, increasing the risk of serious personal injury. By purchasing a ticket and participating, you assume all risks and agree to hold the hosts and venue harmless from any liability or injury.
Minimum of 3 participants for class to run.
Register Now

item.description:
Celebrate the season with U.S. National Scottish Fiddle Champion Seán Heely and a cast of nationally acclaimed performers in a festive journey through the Celtic world. Featuring stirring fiddle and bagpipes, dazzling Scottish and Irish dance, and a rich tapestry of Gaelic carols, traditional tunes, and familiar holiday favorites, this joyful production brings Winter Solstice traditions to life with energy and warmth.

item.title: 40th Annual Winter Faire — Sun Dec 6, 11:00 AM — Susquehanna Waldorf School
item.description:
At Susquehanna Waldorf School, Winter Faire is one of our most cherished traditions—a magical transformation of our school into a place of wonder, warmth, and seasonal delight. Each year, parents, faculty, and staff come together to create an experience rooted in simple joys, meaningful traditions, and the magic of community.
Winter Faire is more than a celebration. It is an opportunity to gather, to play, to create, to share a meal, and to experience the season together. Through the Faire, we also extend that spirit of care beyond our school, supporting a meaningful cause in our wider community, while raising essential funds that help sustain the education and experiences we treasure at SWS.
With great anticipation, we look forward to welcoming you for this special tradition. Come slow down, reconnect, and experience the magic of Winter Faire with us.
Learn More
Source: Fig Lancaster

The CoffeeTue rides are social rides, but cyclists are not expected to stay in one group. Cyclists may pedal at their own comfortable paces. A planned stop to regroup is recommended. Please be supportive of the other cyclists to avoid anyone biking alone or being dropped off the back of the last group. **Be Safe, Have Fun, and Ride Together**

item.description:

The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

Winner of four Best Feature Film awards, The Family Recipe is a fun ensemble comedy about family, tradition, and the beautiful chaos that comes with bringing everyone together under one roof.As Thanksgiving approaches, Alison is determined to host the perfect holiday dinner. But between clashing personalities, long-held grudges, awkward relatives, and one mishap after another, perfection quickly slips out of reach. Filled with warmth, humor, and recognizable family moments, The Family Recipe celebrates the messy traditions that somehow keep families coming back to the table year after year.Trailer

item.title: Evening Compline — Wed Nov 25, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster
